In mathematics, specifically in the field of [[category theory]], the '''associativity isomorphism''' implements the notion of [[Associative property|associativity]] with respect to monoidal products in semi-groupal (or monoidal-without-unit) categories.

== Definition ==

A category, <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, is called semi-groupal if it comes equipped with a [[functor]] <math>\mathcal{C} \times \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{C}</math> such that the pair <math>(A, B) \mapsto A \otimes B</math> for <math>A, B \in \text{ob}(\mathcal{C})</math>, as well as a collection of natural [[Isomorphism|isomorphisms]] known as the '''associativity isomorphisms''' (or "associators").<ref>

== Applications ==
=== In tensor categories ===
A tensor category,<ref>{{cite book
|last1 = Barr
|first1 = Michael
|author-link1=Michael Barr (mathematician)
|last2 = Wells
|first2 =  Charles
|author-link2=Charles Wells (mathematician)
|title = Category Theory for Computing Science| pages = 419}}</ref>{{Full citation needed|date=September 2025}} or [[monoidal category]], is a semi-groupal category with an identity object, <math>I</math>, such that <math>I \otimes A \cong A</math> and <math>A \otimes I \cong A</math>. [[Modular tensor category|modular tensor categories]] have many applications in physics,{{Speculation inline|date=date=September 2025}} especially in the field of topological quantum field theories.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/modular+tensor+category#relation_to_3dcs2dwzw_quantum_field_theory | title = Modular tensor category}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|date=September 2025}}<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rowell |first1=Eric |last2=Stong |first2=Richard |last3=Wang |first3=Zhenghan |title=On Classification of Modular Tensor Categories |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |date=2009 |volume=292 |issue=2 |pages=343–389 |doi=10.1007/s00220-009-0908-z |bibcode=2009CMaPh.292..343R |doi-access=free }}</ref>{{Dubious|date=September 2025}}
